confidence.rationale: Issuer disclosures support repeat buying. No cross-client durability or pricing series.

advantage.rationale: Specialized integration and multi-market technology delivery evidenced by the Airbus multi-year strategic IT agreement after about a decade of business; Japanese joint-venture channels corroborate delivery capability.

behavior.rationale: Airbus extended an established relationship into a multi-year agreement. FY customers generating at least USD 1m rose 251 to 266.

proxy.interpretation: Renewed customer commitment after repeat service and integrated implementation evidence support technological differentiation and possible switching friction.
proxy.limitation: No measured churn, switching cost, renewal rate, winning prices or client-cohort monetization. Customer threshold counts and project wins do not identify renewals.

persistence.rationale: A longstanding and extended relationship shows persistence in that example. Breadth of durability and economics across customers remains uncertain.

counter.rationale: Labor costs, delivery mix and competing suppliers limit inference about pricing power. Data do not demonstrate broad renewals or pricing protection.

changes.impact: Q1 trading remained active. H1 and 9M large-project wins show buyers still choose FPT for complex technology work.
9M international IT margin of 15.32% corroborates commercial viability. Mix and labor constrain relative pricing claims.
Large-award counts show commercial traction. They cannot establish realized profitability or repeat-buying rates by themselves.
Consolidation boundary changed capital reporting. The customer contract/delivery assessment does not depend on group funded capital.
Leverage remains separate financial context. No retained evidence connects the reported change to loss of delivery capacity or customer access.
Telecom composition changed. The supported band rests on observed technology-services behavior.
Equity accounting for FTEL changes scope and financial ratios. Technology service buying and delivery are corroborated by eligible post-transition awards.
FTEL change is documented; no further loss of the specific technology mechanism was established in the reviewed event set.
Exclude scope-mixed group margins and return comparisons from moat proof.
The observed customer mechanism uses no WACC or ROIC inference.
AI may erode delivery/pricing advantages; AI and SBI developments provide no measured margin or retention benefit. 9M competitive wins support the existing limited differentiation band.

continuedApplicability.rationale: Fresh large awards support differentiation despite insufficient repeat-order and pricing detail for a higher band.

Award counts are cumulative and are not recognized revenue.
No verified relative cost leadership, widespread pricing power or telecom moat is claimed.
